How the City Budget Works: Guide for New Staff This page is part of the onboarding wiki of the Finance Directorate, Municipality of Brașov. It gives new staff a practical overview of the annual budget cycle, the main documents and the people involved. It is not a legal reference; for legal questions, consult th

e legal department or Law No. 273/2006 on local public finance. Page owner: Silvia Neagoe, head of the budget office. The Annual Cycle The municipal budget runs from 1 January to 31 December. Preparation starts in the summer, when the Min
istry of Finance publishes the budget framework letter with estimates of shared tax revenues and the timetable for the next year. Departments submit their proposals to our office in September and October. The draft budget is published for public consultation for at least 15 days, then debated by the local council's specialised committees and adopted, usually in late January or February, once the national budget law has been passed. Who Does What - The budget office collects proposals, checks them against revenue estimates and prepares the draft. - Department heads justify their spending requests and attend committee hearings. - The mayor presents the draft to the council and decides on priorities when requests exceed revenues. - The local council debates, amends and adopts the budget by majority vote.
- The internal audit service reviews execution and reports to the council once a year. Key Documents The budget itself has two main sections. The operating section covers salaries, utilities, maintenance and subsidies, while the development section covers investments such as roads, schools and the new tram line to the industrial park. Each department's spending is broken down by economic classification, such as goods and services or capital expenditure, and by functional classification, such as education or transport. New staff often find the classifications confusing at first; the budget office keeps a printed cheat sheet in the shared folder Bugete/Ghiduri. During the Year

Once adopted, the budget can be amended through rectifications, which also require a council vote. In 2025, the council approved three rectifications, the largest in July, when additional EU funds for the energy renovation of schools were received. Departments monitor their spending in the Forexebug system linked to the State Treasury, and monthly execution reports are sent to the mayor's office by the tenth day of the following month. Common Questions New staff often as
k whether unspent money can be carried over. In general it cannot: unspent operating appropriations lapse at year-end, except for certain EU-funded projects. If you think a
project may not spend its allocation, talk to the budget office early so the money can be reallocated during a rectification rather than lost.

The Nineteenth Dynasty of Egypt (notated Dynasty XIX), also known as the Ramessid dynast
y, is classified as the second Dynasty of the Ancient Egyptian New Kingdom period,
 lasting from 1292 BC to 1189 BC. The 19th Dynasty and the 20th D
ynasty furthermore together constitute an era known as the Ramesside period. This Dynasty was founded by Vizier Ramesses I, whom Pharaoh Horemheb chose as his successor to the throne. History Background
The warrior kings of the early 18th Dynasty had encountered only little resistance from neighbouring kingdoms, allowing them to expand their realm of influence easily, but the international situation had changed radically towards the end of the dynasty. The Hittites had gradually extended their influence into Syria and Canaan to become a major power in international politics, a power that both Seti I and his son Ramesses II would confront in the future. 19th Dynasty Seti I and Ramesses 

II The New Kingdom of Egypt reached the zenith of its power under Seti I and Ramesses II ("The Grea
t"), who campaigned vigorously against the Libyans and the Hittites. The city of Kadesh was first captured by Seti I, who decided to concede it to Muwatalli of Hatti in an informal peace treaty between Egypt and Hatti. Ramesses II later attempted unsuccessfully to alter this situation in his fifth regnal year by launching an attack on Kadesh in his Second Syrian campaign in 1274 BC; he was caught in history's first recorded military ambush, but thanks to the arrival of the Ne'arin (a force allied with Egypt), Ramesses was able to rally his troops and turn the tide of battle against the Hittites. Ramesses II later profited from the Hittites' interna
l difficulties, during his eighth and ninth regnal years, when he campaigned against their Syrian possessions, capturing Kadesh and portions of Southern Syria, and advanci
ng as far north as Tunip, where no Egyptian soldier had been seen for 120 years. He ultimately accepted that a campaign against the Hittites was an unsupportable drain on Egypt's treasury and military. In his 21st regnal year, Ramesses signed the earliest recorded peace treaty with Urhi-Teshub's successor, Hattusili III, and with that act Egypt-Hittite relations improved significantly. Ramesses II even married two Hittite princesses, the first after his second Sed Festival.

Merneptah and successors This dynasty declined as infighting for the throne between the heirs of Merneptah increased. Amenmesse apparently usurped the throne from Merneptah's son and successor, Seti II, but he ruled Egypt for
only four years. After his death, Seti regained power and destroyed most of Amenmesse's monuments. Seti was served at court by Chancellor Bay, who was originally just a 'royal scribe' but quickly became one of the most powerful men in Egypt, gaining the unprecedented privilege of constructing his own tomb in the Valley of the Kings (KV13). Both Bay and Seti's chief wife, Twosret, had a sinister reputation in Ancient Egyptian folklore. After Siptah's death, Twosret ruled Egypt for two more years, but she proved unable to maintain her hold on power amid the conspiracies and powerplays being hatched at the royal court. She was likely ousted in a revolt led by Setnakhte, founder of the 20th Dynasty. Pharaohs of the 19th Dynasty The pharaohs of the 19th Dynasty ruled for approximately 110 years: from to 1187 BC. Many of the pharaohs were buried in the Valley of the Kings in Thebes (designated KV). More information can be found on the Theban Mapping Project website.

County Road 350 () is a road in the municipality of Heim in Trøndelag county, Norway. The road branches off from European route E39 at the Åsletten farm in Halsa and runs a short distance north to Halsa Church, and then north-northeast until it 
nears Klevset on the shore of Skålvik Fjord. There it turns north-northwest and passes through Rabben and Setra before terminating at Korneset on the shore of Vinje Fjord, where a local road continues, circling around the Halsa Peninsula and eventually leading back to Halsa.

The county road and the smaller local road are also both named Halsavegen (Halsa Road).

Changelog for the Western Indian
 Ocean Reef Monitoring Protocol Maintained by the regional coordination office at the Kenya Marine and Fisheries Research Institute, Mombasa. This document records changes to the shared survey prot
ocol used by monitoring teams in Kenya, Tanzania, Mozambique and the Seychelles. Each entry gives the version, t
he date it took effect, and a short explanation so that teams comparing data across years can understand where methods differ. Version 3.2, effective 1 January 2027 * Raised the minimum number of transects per site from three to four * Added sea urchin counts to the invertebrate belt survey * Split the "algae" benthic category into turf, macroalgae and crustose coralline algae * Required water temperature loggers at all sentinel sites The extra transect was added after a statistical review by Dr Halima Mwakio found that three transects gave too much variation to detect changes in coral cover of less than five percentage points. Splitting the algae category reflects growing interest in how different algae types affect coral recovery; crustose coralline algae help young corals settle, while thick macroalgae can smother them. Teams comparing older data should merge the three new categories back into one.

Version 3.1, effective 1 March 2025 * Introduced a bleaching severity scale with five levels, replacing the previous yes or no record * Allowed photo quadrats as an alternative to point-intercept for sites deeper than 15 metres * Standardised fish size classes at 5-centimetre intervals up to 40 centimetres

The bleaching scale was the most important change in this version. During the 2024 event, several teams recorded colonies as "bleached" without distinguishing slight paling from complete whitening, making it impossible to compare severity between countries. The new scale was tested by teams in Watamu and Zanzibar before adoption. Version 3.0, effective 1 January 2023 * Merged the separate Kenyan and Tanzanian protocols into one regional standard * Adopted 20-metre transect length across all countries * Moved all data entry to the shared online database Before 2023, Kenyan teams used 30-metre transects and Tanzanian teams used 20-metre transects, which complicated regional comparisons. The shorter length was chosen because it fits more easily on narrow fringing reefs common in Mozambique. Notes for Data Users When combining data across vers
ions, always check the protocol version recorded with each survey. The database flags any record collected
 under an older version, and conversion notes are available from the coordination office. Questions about changes should be sent to the protocol committee, chaired this year
by Mr Omar Abdalla of the Seychelles Fishing Authority.

This document records changes to the shared survey protocol used by monitoring teams in Kenya, Tanzania, Mozambique and the Seychelles. Each entry gives the version, the date it took effect, and a short explanation so that teams comparing data across years can understand where methods differ.

Version 3.2, effective 1 January 2027

* Raised the minimum number of transects per site from three to four
* Added sea urchin counts to the invertebrate belt survey
* Split the "algae" benthic category into turf, macroalgae and crustose coralline algae
* Required water temperature loggers at all sentinel sites

The extra transect was added after a statistical review by Dr Halima Mwakio found that three transects gave too much variation to detect changes in coral cover of less than five percentage points. Splitting the algae category reflects growing interest in how different algae types affect coral recovery; crustose coralline algae help young corals settle, while thick macroalgae can smother them. Teams comparing older data should merge the three new categories back into one.

Version 3.1, effective 1 March 2025

* Introduced a bleaching severity scale with five levels, replacing the previous yes or no record
* Allowed photo quadrats as an alternative to point-intercept for sites deeper than 15 metres
* Standardised fish size classes at 5-centimetre intervals up to 40 centimetres

The bleaching scale was the most important change in this version. During the 2024 event, several teams recorded colonies as "bleached" without distinguishing slight paling from complete whitening, making it impossible to compare severity between countries. The new scale was tested by teams in Watamu and Zanzibar before adoption.

Version 3.0, effective 1 January 2023

* Merged the separate Kenyan and Tanzanian protocols into one regional standard
* Adopted 20-metre transect length across all countries
* Moved all data entry to the shared online database

Before 2023, Kenyan teams used 30-metre transects and Tanzanian teams used 20-metre transects, which complicated regional comparisons. The shorter length was chosen because it fits more easily on narrow fringing reefs common in Mozambique.

Notes for Data Users

When combining data across versions, always check the protocol version recorded with each survey. The database flags any record collected under an older version, and conversion notes are available from the coordination office. input: Nicolaes Woutersz van der Meer (1575 – 1666) was a Dutch brewer, magistrate and mayor of Haarlem, best known today for his portrait with its pendant of his wife Cornelia Claesdr Voogt, both painted by Frans Hals in 1631. Biography He was born in Haarlem as the son of Wouter Claes Woutersz and Maria Adriaensdr van der Meer. He was first called Nicolaes Woutersz and later added his mother's surname. In 1607 he became a member of the Haarlem regency. In 1619 he became a member of the Admiralty of Amsterdam, and in 1622 he became a representative to the States-General of the Netherlands for Haarlem. Though he is known for his wedding portrait with its pendant, Van der Meer was also portrayed as Captain of the St Jorisschutterij in Hals' The Banquet of the Officers of the St George Militia Company in 1616. These pendant portraits were painted on oak panels and after these, Hals switched to canvas and oak panel became more rare in his oeuvre. The pendants came into the possession of the Frans Hals Museum in 1883, when they were left in the estate of J.C.W. Fabricius van Leyenburg. His wife Cornelia Claesdr Voogt was a member of the Haarlem brewer family Voogt. Her brother Willem Claesz Vooght ran the Voogt brewery on the "Coude Horn", and her sister Maritge was married to the Haarlem brewer Pieter Jacobsz Olycan, all three of whom were also painted by Hals.

His wife Cornelia Claesdr Voogt was a member of the Haarlem brewer family Voogt. Her brother Willem Claesz Vooght ran the Voogt brewery on the "Coude Horn", and her sister Maritge was married to the Haarlem brewer Pieter Jacobsz Olycan, all three of whom were also painted by Hals.

August William Derleth (February 24, 1909 – July 4, 1971) was an American writer and anthologist. He was the first book publisher of the writings of H. P. Lovecraft. He made contrib
utions to the Cthulhu Mythos and the cosmic horror genre and helped f
ound the publisher Arkham House (which did much to bring supernatural fiction into print in hardcover in the US that had o
nly been readily available in the UK). Derleth was also a leading American regional
 writer of his day, as well as prolific in several other genres, including historical fiction, poetry, detective fiction, science fiction, and biogra
phy. Notably, he created the fictional detective Solar Pons, a pastiche of Arthur Conan Doyle's Sherlock Holmes. A 1938 Guggenheim Fellow, Derleth
 considered his most serious work to be the ambitious Sac Prairie Saga, a series of fiction, historical fiction, poetry, and non-fiction naturalist works designed to memorialize life in the Wisconsin he knew. Derleth can also be considered a pioneering naturalist and conservationist
in his writing. 

Life The son of William Julius Derleth and Rose Louise Volk, Derleth grew up in Sauk City, Wisconsin. He was educated in local parochial and public high school. Derleth wrote his first fiction at age 13. He was interested most in reading, and he made three trips to the library a week. He would save his money to buy books (his personal l
ibrary exceeded 12,000 volumes later on in life). Some of his biggest influences were Ralph Waldo
 Emerson's essays, Walt Whitman, H. L. Mencken's The American Mercury, Samuel Johnson's The Histo
ry of Rasselas, Prince of Abissinia, Alexandre Dumas, Edgar Allan Poe, Walter Scott, and Henry David Thoreau's Walden. Forty rejected stories and three years later, according to anthologist Jim Stephens, he sold his first story, "Bat's Belfry", to Weird Tales magazine in 1926. Derleth wrote throughout his four years at the University of Wisconsin, where he received a B.A. in 1930. During this time he also served briefly as associate editor of Minneapolis-based Fawcett Publications Mystic Magazine. Returning to Sauk City 
in the summer of 1931, Derleth worked in a local canning factory and collaborated with childhood friend Mark Schorer (later Chairman of the University of California, Berkeley English Department). They rented a cabin, writing Gothic and other horror stories and selling them to Weird Tales magazine. Derleth won a place on the O'Brien Roll of Honor for Five Alone, published in Place of Hawks, but was first published in Pagany magazin
e. As a result of his early work on the Sac Prairie Saga, Derleth was awarded the prestigious Guggenheim Fellowship; his sponsors were Helen C. White, Nobel Prize-winning novelist Sinclair Lewis and poet Edgar Lee Masters of Spoon River Anthology fame. In the mid-1930s, Derleth organized a Ranger's Club for young people, served as clerk and president of the local school board, served as a parole officer, organized a local men's club and a parent-teacher association. He also lectured in American regional literature at the University of Wisconsin and was a contributing editor of Outdoors Magazine. With longtime friend Donald Wandrei, Derleth founded Arkham
House in 1939. Its initial objective was to publish the works of H. P. Lovecraft, with whom Derleth had corresponded since his teenage years. At the same time, he began teaching a course in American Regional Literature at the University of Wisconsin.

Pippo Delbono (born 1 June 1959 in Varazze, Italy) is an Italian author, actor, and director. Biography Pippo Delbono began training in traditional theatre in Denmark, studying the principles of oriental theatre, 

through a rigorous work on body and voice. Later, in Germany, Delbono was invited by Pina Bausch to follow her work. At the beginning of the 80's he founded the Compagnia Pippo Delbono, creating most of his works with them, from Il Tempo degli Assassini (1987) to La Gioia (2018). He does not stage plays but, rather, total creations, devised with a stable group of actors whose number has grown through the years. The encounter with socially marginalized people determines a turning point in his poetical research: that's how Barboni (1997) was born. Some of these actors – among them Bobò, deaf-mute, who had been kept in an asylum in Aversa, near Naples, for forty-five years and recently died – have kept working with the company and are still a central part of this experience. The works that followed — La rabbia dedicated to Pasolini, Guerra, Esodo, Gente di plastica, Racconti di giugno, Urlo, Il silenzio, Questo buio feroce, La menzogna, Dopo la battaglia, Orchidee, Vangelo, La gioia — like the ones before, have been performed worldwide in more than fifty countries, in theaters and festivals, including the Festival d'Avignon (where a lot of the company's creations were p
resented), Barcelona's Grec
, Theater Spektakel in Zurich, Festwochen in Wien, Festival TransAmeriques in Montreal, Venice Biennale, etc. In 2009, he was awarded the Europe Prize Theatrical Realities, in Wrocław. Several theatres, including the Théâtre du Rond-Point in Paris, Piccolo Teatro in Milan, Teatro Argentina in Rome, among others, present regularly his performances. Henry V — his only creation based on an existing play – is the only Italian production of Shakespeare that has ever been invited to
perform at the Royal Shakespeare Company. His production Vangelo (2016) 

has been realized at Croatian National Theatre in Zagreb with actors of
 his company together with Croatian actors, dancers, musicians and chorus and with refugees of the PIAM refugee camp in Asti (Italy). The performance has two
versions: Opera with chorus and orchestra, that premiered in Italy at Teatro Comunale in Bologna, and Drama version, that premiered at Thèatre Vidy – Lausanne. The music of the performance are by Enzo Avitabile who won the Ubu Prize for them. His last theatre creation, La gioia, premiered in March 2018 and has been presented at Theatre Olympics
in Delhi and Bhopal (India), at Hong Kong Arts Festival, in Shizuoka (Japan), in Tunisia, Spain, Portugal. and it will be on tour in the theatrical season 2021/2022. Europe Theatre Prize In 2009, he was one of the recipients of the XI Europe
 Prize Theatrical Realities. The prize organization described Delbono as a "
poet of social marginalisation and diversity" and stated that he "has always seen art as a fundamental experience for overcoming desperation". Theatre Opera Studio per Obra Maestra at Teatro Lirico Sperimentale Spoleto (2007)
Cavalleria Rusticana by Pietro Mascagni at Teatro di San Carlo Naples (2012) Don Giovanni by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart at Grand Theatre, Poznań (2014) Madama Butterfly by Giacomo Puccini at Teatro di San Carlo Naples (2014 and 2016) St John Passion by Johann Sebastian Bach at Teatro Massimo Palermo Pagliacci by Ruggero Leoncavallo at Teatro dell'Opera di Roma (2018)

Tōtara Bank app outage blamed on rushed update, bank admits Customer
s of Tōtara Bank were locked out of the bank's mobile app for nearly nine hours on Wednesday after an update released that morning prevented thousands of users from logging in, the bank has confirmed. The problems began shortly after 7 am, when v
ersion 8.4 of the app became available through the Apple App Store and Google Play. Within an hour, Tōtara Bank's customer service lines were overwhelmed with calls, and the hashtag for the bank was trending on social media in New Zealand. Customers reported being unable to
 check balances, transfer money or pay 
bills, and some were caught out at supermarket checkouts after relying on the app to move funds. What Went Wrong In a statement released on Thursday afternoon, Tōtara Bank's chief digital officer, Simone Harcourt, said the update

 had changed how the app communicated with the bank's login system. A configuration setting that worked correctly in testing had not been updated on the production servers before the release went live. Harcourt said the bank had identified several failings in the release process: 1. The update was released to all customers at once rather than in stages.
2. The production server change was

scheduled for the evening rather than before the release. 3. Testing used a staging environment that did not match production settings exactly. 4. The team did not have a quick way to disable the new login process once problems 
emerged. "We let our customers down, and I'm sorry," Harcourt said. "Our process should
have caught this, and it didn't." Customer Frustration Wellington café owner Tama Rowe said he lost the ability to pay suppliers on one of his busiest days. "I had deliveries arriving and couldn't pay anyone," he said. "I ended up driving to the branch on Willis Street, and there was a queue out the door." Online
banking through a web browser continued to work throughout the outage, but many customers did not re 
alise this was an option. Industry Response Software engineering lecturer Dr Ngaio Templeton of the University of Canterbury said the incident followed a familiar pattern. Staged releases, where an update goes to a small percentage of users first, are now standard practice in large app development teams because they limit the damage when something goes wrong. She noted that mobile apps cannot easily be rolled back once installed, which makes caution during release particularly important. The bank said it would compensate customers who incurred late payment fees or dishonour charges as a direct result of the outage. Customers can apply through the bank's website, and claims will be accepted until 31 October. The Banking Ombudsman said it had received 46 inquiries about the outage by Thursday evening.

Tōtara Bank app outage blamed on rushed update, bank admits

Customers of Tōtara Bank were locked out of the bank's mobile app for nearly nine hours on Wednesday after an update released that morning prevented thousands of users from logging in, the bank has confirmed.

The problems began shortly after 7 am, when version 8.4 of the app became available through the Apple App Store and Google Play. Within an hour, Tōtara Bank's customer service lines were overwhelmed with calls, and the hashtag for the bank was trending on social media in New Zealand. Customers reported being unable to check balances, transfer money or pay bills, and some were caught out at supermarket checkouts after relying on the app to move funds.

What Went Wrong

In a statement released on Thursday afternoon, Tōtara Bank's chief digital officer, Simone Harcourt, said the update had changed how the app communicated with the bank's login system. A configuration setting that worked correctly in testing had not been updated on the production servers before the release went live.

Harcourt said the bank had identified several failings in the release process:

1. The update was released to all customers at once rather than in stages.
2. The production server change was scheduled for the evening rather than before the release.
3. Testing used a staging environment that did not match production settings exactly.
4. The team did not have a quick way to disable the new login process once problems emerged.

"We let our customers down, and I'm sorry," Harcourt said. "Our process should have caught this, and it didn't."

Customer Frustration

Wellington café owner Tama Rowe said he lost the ability to pay suppliers on one of his busiest days. "I had deliveries arriving and couldn't pay anyone," he said. "I ended up driving to the branch on Willis Street, and there was a queue out the door." Online banking through a web browser continued to work throughout the outage, but many customers did not realise this was an option.

Industry Response

Software engineering lecturer Dr Ngaio Templeton of the University of Canterbury said the incident followed a familiar pattern. Staged releases, where an update goes to a small percentage of users first, are now standard practice in large app development teams because they limit the damage when something goes wrong. She noted that mobile apps cannot easily be rolled back once installed, which makes caution during release particularly important.

The bank said it would compensate customers who incurred late payment fees or dishonour charges as a direct result of the outage. Customers can apply through the bank's website, and claims will be accepted until 31 October. The Banking Ombudsman said it had received 46 inquiries about the outage by Thursday evening.

3 Study Area and Survey Design

Our surveys were conducted on the fringing reefs of Amami Oshima, the largest island of the Amami archipelago in Kagoshima prefecture, between June 2024 and July 2026. Amami lies near the northern limit of extensive coral reef development in the western Pacific and experiences both summer heat stress and winter cooling, making it a useful location for studying how reef communities respond to repeated disturbance at the edge of their range.

3.1 Site Selection

We selected twelve sites distributed around the island to capture gradients in wave exposure, river influence and tourism pressure. Sites were chosen using the reef maps published by the Ministry of the Environment in 2018, supplemented by local knowledge from fishers and dive operators in Naze and Setouchi. The sites fall into three groups:

* Four exposed sites on the eastern Pacific-facing coast with strong wave action
* Four sheltered sites in Oshima Strait, sheltered from waves but affected by boat traffic
* Four sites near river mouths on the western coast, receiving sediment after heavy rain

Each site was surveyed at two depths, 3 metres and 8 metres, to distinguish shallow reef flat and slope communities.

3.2 Field Methods

At each site and depth we laid three permanent 30-metre transects marked with stainless steel stakes. Benthic cover was recorded by photographing a 50 by 50 centimetre quadrat every metre along each transect, giving 90 images per site and depth. Juvenile corals smaller than 5 centimetres were counted in 1-metre belt transects. Divers Kaito Yasuda and Shino Arima, both trained in the Coral Watch protocol, carried out all surveys to minimise observer differences.

Temperature loggers recording at 30-minute intervals were attached to the stakes at every station. Sediment traps were deployed at the river-influenced sites for two weeks during each survey period and analysed for total deposition and organic content at the Amami field station of Kagoshima University.

3.3 Image Analysis

Quadrat photographs were analysed by random point annotation, with 50 points per image classified into hard coral genera, soft coral, turf algae, macroalgae, crustose coralline algae, sand and other categories. Annotation was performed by two analysts, and a subset of 400 images was annotated by both to estimate agreement, which reached a kappa of 0.84 for major categories.

3.4 Disturbance Events

During the study, Amami experienced a severe marine heatwave in August 2024 and the passage of Typhoon Shanshan in late August 2024, which brought strong swell to the eastern coast. These events allow the comparison of thermal and physical disturbance across site groups, which forms the basis of the analyses in section 4.

Tsun-Peng Pao (1916–1970), also known by his courtesy name Longxi, was a journalist, writer and government official who served as the first director of the National Museum of History in the Republic of China.

Early life and education Pao was born on November 2, 1916, in Dingyuan County, Anhui Province, China. He graduated from Fudan University, National Chengchi University, and the Central School of Party Affairs. He also conducted research at the University of Pennsylvania in the United States Career
In late 1948, Pao moved to Taiwan and taught at several universities, including National Taiwan Normal University, Soochow University, Fu Jen Catholic University, and
 the Chinese Culture University. He was also involved in cultural and academic activities.

In 1955, Pao became the preparatory director of the National Museum of History and served as its director from 1956 to 1969. In 1968, he was appointed as the director of the National Central Library (now known as the National Library of Taiwan).Pao's scholarly work focused on the history and development of museums in China, as well as the preservation of cultural artifacts. Some of his notable writings include "A Draft History of Chinese Museums," "The Evolution and Development of Chinese Museums," "On Historical Museums," "The Preservation of Cultural Relics during Wartime," "The Law on the Protection of Cultural Relics," and "The Preservation of Outdoor Museums and Historic Sites." Death
During his time in public service, Pao's health deteriorated. He died on February 20, 1970, at the age of 55 at Tri-Service General Hospital in Taipei.

ath by a stranger with a hunting knife outside her home in the vicinity of Irvington Avenue and Prince Street near the Elizabeth River in a then-upscale a
rea of Elizabeth, New Jersey.
Her murderer, despite witnesses, was never identified.

 her coat.

Initially, the child thought she had been punched in the abdomen and cried out in pain. Her assailant kept walking. A witness to the stabbing told The New York Times in 1995 her recollection of the attack: "[The witness said she] was walking with her niece about 20 feet in front of Wendy when a large man wearing a dark corduroy coat and a blue or gray fedora hat approached her and asked for directions. "He asked me 'How do you get

he had been stabbed. Wendy was rushed to Elizabeth General Hospital, where she shortly passed away. Description of killer

Same-day assaults on other girls

Streets
. Shortly before that, on the same day, he was thought to have stabbed a young Elizabeth girl named Patricia in the backside at Spring Street and Elizabeth Avenue; she made a full recovery, although some initial confusion over the attacker's identity occurred. Additionally, he was though

ified the community. Authorities questioned more than 1,500 men, searched prisons and mental institutions in 13 states, and examined a military ship docked in the port of Elizabeth before it left for Vietnam. “They must have rousted every bum out of every rooming house in town," said one contemporary investigator. residents reca

Despite extensive investigations and public appeals, the identity of the perpetrator remained unknown. Physical evidence The murder weapon, a hunting knife, was discovered near the site. des, reports say it had gone missing from evidence storage.

Murder
On March 8, 1966, at around 4pm, seven-year-old Wendy walked near the front of her Pierce Manor apartment building to meet her mother, who was bringing the car around from its parking area near their home. At the time, the Pierce Manor Apartments was an upscale building complex in an affluent area of the city (Westminster). The two were to run errands and pick up Wendy's older sister Jodi from Hebrew school.
A middle-aged man appeared walking in the opposite direction from Wendy, suddenly crouched down, and stabbed her in the abdomen through her coat.

Initially, the child thought she had been punched in the abdomen and cried out in pain. Her assailant kept walking.

A witness to the stabbing told The New York Times in 1995 her recollection of the attack:

"[The witness said she] was walking with her niece about 20 feet in front of Wendy when a large man wearing a dark corduroy coat and a blue or gray fedora hat approached her and asked for directions.

"He asked me 'How do you get downtown?' Then he walked past me, and I turned around and I looked for my niece. And I saw him bent over this little girl," the woman said. "I said to the little girl 'What is the matter?' She said 'He punched me, the man punched me."

The woman said she did not realize the girl had been stabbed. But because Wendy was obviously in pain, she brought her to a nearby firehouse.

At the Elizabeth Fire Department building across the street, personnel realized she had been stabbed. Wendy was rushed to Elizabeth General Hospital, where she shortly passed away.

Description of killer
Three young female witnesses described the killer as being around 6 feet tall and weighing around 220lbs. He appeared white and around 45 to 50 years old with gray hair and a slight limp.

Witnesses also reported that the man's face was "extremely pale" and "lifeless."

Same-day assaults on other girls
The assailant was suspected in assaults against other Elizabeth schoolgirls that occurred only minutes earlier and less than a mile from where Wendy was killed, according to investigators. Minutes earlier, without provocation, he was thought to have hauled off and punched a seventh-grade Catholic schoolgirl named Diane in the eye, knocking her onto the ground in front of shocked witnesses at Broad and West Jersey Streets. Shortly before that, on the same day, he was thought to have stabbed a young Elizabeth girl named Patricia in the backside at Spring Street and Elizabeth Avenue; she made a full recovery, although some initial confusion over the attacker's identity occurred. Additionally, he was thought to have put his arms around a 16-year- old girl at Morris Avenue and Prince Street prior to attacking Wendy.

Investigation

Contemporary investigation
The murder shocked and terrified the community.
Authorities questioned more than 1,500 men, searched prisons and mental institutions in 13 states, and examined a military ship docked in the port of Elizabeth before it left for Vietnam. “They must have rousted every bum out of every rooming house in town," said one contemporary investigator.

Many contemporary residents recalled the child's death as marking an "end of innocence" and a change in their estimation in the sense of safety and middle-class comforts in the city.

Despite extensive investigations and public appeals, the identity of the perpetrator remained unknown.

Physical evidence
The murder weapon, a hunting knife, was discovered near the site. In later decades, reports say it had gone missing from evidence storage.

Barratry ( ) is a legal term that, at common law, described a criminal offense committed by people who are overly officious in instigat
ing or encouraging prosecution of groundless litigation, or who bring repeated or persistent acts of litigation for the purposes of profit or harassm
ent. Although it remains a crime in some jurisdictions, barratry has frequently been abolished as being anachronistic and obsolete. Bar
ratry by countr
y Australia In Australia, the term barratry is predominantly used in the first sense of a frivolous or harassing litigant. The concept has fallen into disuse in Australia. New South Wales The offence of being a common barrator was abolished in New South Wales by Section 4A of the Maintenance, Champerty and Barratry Abolition Act 1993. Victoria
The o
ffence of being a common barrator was abolished in Victoria by section 2 of the Abolition of Obsolete Offences Act 1969. Canada In Canada, barratry, alongside all common law offences except contempt of court, were abolished by the 1953 consolidation of the Criminal Code. United Kingdom England and Wales
In England and Wales the common law offence of being a common barrator was abolished by section 13(1)(a) of the Criminal Law Act 1967. History Being a common barrator was an offence under the common law of England. It was classified as a misdemeanor. It consisted of "persistently stirring up quarrels in the Courts or out of them". It is uncertain whether, in th
e ordinary way, persons charged with commission of the offence were dealt with by
 indictment. In 1966, the Law Commission recommended for the offence to be abolished. It said that there had been no indictments for this offence for "many years" and that, as an indictable misdemeanor, it was "wholly obsolete". I
ts recommendation was impleme
nted by the Criminal Law Act 1967. Scotland In Scots law, barra
try referred to the crime committed by a judge who is induced by bribery to pronounce judgment. United States Several jurisdictions in the United States have declared barratry (in the sense of a frivolous or harassing litigant) to be a crime as part of their tort reform efforts. For example, in the U.S. states of California, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, Virginia, and Washington, barratry is a misdemeanor. In Texas, barratry is a misdemeanor on the first conviction, but a felony on subsequent convictions. California Penal Code Section 158: "Common barratry is the practice of exciting groundless judicial proceedings, and is punishable by imprisonment in the county jail not exceeding six months and by fine not exceeding one thousand dollars ($
1,000)." California Penal Code Section 159: "No person can be convicted of common barratry except upon proof that he has excited suits or proceedings at law in at least three instances, and with a corrupt or malicious intent to vex and annoy." Revised Code of Washington 9.12.010: "Every person who brings on his or her own behalf, or instigates, incites, or encourages another to bring, 
any false suit at law or in equity in any court of this state, with intent thereby to distress or harass a defendant in the suit, or who serves
 or sends any paper or document purporting to be or resembling a 
judicial process, that is not in fact a judicial process, is guilty of a misdemeanor; and in case the person
 offending is an attorney, he or she may, in addition thereto be disbarred from practicing law within this state." Virginia laws on barratry, champerty, and maintenance were overturned by the Supreme Court of the United States in NAACP v. Button 371 U.S. 415 (1963). Vermont Statutes Title 13, § 701: "A person who is a common barrator shall be fined not more th
an $50.00 and become bound with sufficient surety for his or her good behavior for not less than one year."

WindOps Platform: Release Notes for Turbine Maintenance Modules

WindOps is the maintenance management platform used by operators of onshore wind farms in Korea and Vietnam. These notes describe changes to the maintenance scheduling and inspection modules in recent releases and explain the reasoning, so that site managers can adjust their workflows. Release 12.3, 22 September 2026 1. Added a lightning strike log that links SCADA lightning alarms to automatic blade inspection work orders. 2. Introduced a typhoon preparation checklist, triggered when the national weather service issues a typhoon advisory for the farm's location. 3. Changed the default interval for yaw gear lubrication from six months to four months for turbines installed after 2020. 4. Fixed an error that counted cancelled work orders in the monthly availability report. The lightning log was requested by the operations team at Tuy Phong in Binh Thuan province, where thunderstorms between May and October regularly strike turbines. Previously, technicians had to search SCADA alarms manually to decide which blades needed inspection, and two damaged receptors went unnoticed 
for several weeks in 2025. Ms. 
Nguyen Thi Thu Ha, maintenance planner at the site, estimated that automatic work orders save about six hours of planning time per storm. The typhoon checklist covers securing nacelle hatches, checking yaw brakes and confirming that turbines will feather correctly if grid power is lost. Release 12.2, 6 July 2026 1. Introduced a spare parts forecast based on component age and historical failure rates.
2. Allowed technicians to attach thermal camera images directly to inspection records from tablets.
3. Added Vietnamese language support for technician screens. The spare parts forecast addresses long lead times for components such as pitch bearings and main shaft seals, which can take four to six months to arrive from Europe. The model uses
 each farm's own failure history where enough data exist and industry averages otherwise. Mr. Ji Sung-hoon, asset manager at a farm in Yeongyang, said the first forecast helped him order converter modules three months earlier than he would otherwise have done.

Release 12.1, 30 April 2026 1. Rebuilt the scheduling engine to account for wind forecasts when planning climbs. 2. Added a crane booking calendar shared between farms owned by the same operator. Technicians cannot safely climb turbines when wind speeds exceed about 15 metres per second, so planning climbs on calm days is critical. The new engine reads three-day forecasts and moves non-urgent climbs to suitable days automatically, with managers approving the changes. Known Issues

The typhoon checklist does not yet
recognise advisories issued by Vietnamese authorities in their newest format; a fix is planned for release 12.4. Contact support through the platform for help.

Mr. Ji Sung-hoon, asset manager at a farm in Yeongyang, said the first forecast helped him order converter modules three months earlier than he would otherwise have done.

Release 12.1, 30 April 2026

1. Rebuilt the scheduling engine to account for wind forecasts when planning climbs.
2. Added a crane booking calendar shared between farms owned by the same operator.

Technicians cannot safely climb turbines when wind speeds exceed about 15 metres per second, so planning climbs on calm days is critical. The new engine reads three-day forecasts and moves non-urgent climbs to suitable days automatically, with managers approving the changes.

Known Issues

The typhoon checklist does not yet recognise advisories issued by Vietnamese authorities in their newest format; a fix is planned for release 12.4. Contact support through the platform for help.

CI-1017 is a muscarinic acetylcholine receptor agonist which is selective for and is approximat
ely equipotent at the M1 and M4 receptors, with 20-30-fold lower affinity for the M2, M3, and M5 subtypes It is the (R)-enantiomer of the racemic compound PD-142,505. In animals CI-1017 improves learning and memory and increases the electrical activity of the hippocampus through activation of the M1 receptor, while minimally producing parasympathetic side effects and only at very high doses. It also inhibits production of amyloidogenic A beta peptide and increases secretion of soluble amyloid precursor protein via stimulation of the M1 receptor as well. Based on these data, it was hypothesized that CI-1017 could not only treat the symptoms of Alzheimer's disease, but could also potentially slow its progression. It was tested in clinical trials for this purpose in the early 2000s but was abandoned due to lack of efficacy.

Description The shell of this species is unusual in that it has a double series of long, curved spines on the posterior slope of each valve. A closely related species which occurs in the Western Atlantic is Pitar dione.

Distribution
This species is found in the Eastern Pacific Ocean.

g and Technology in 2016, and as an IEEE Fellow, in the 2020 class of fellows, "for contributions to resource allocation and optimization in wireless communications". She is also a Distinguished Lecturer of the IEEE Communications Society.

Legal Opinion Summary: Copyright Status of Attention-Based Language Model Weights

Prepared for the board of IntelSur Tecnología S.A., Buenos Aires, by its external counsel, 25 August 2026

Question Presented

IntelSur has trained a transformer language model for Spanish legal documents, relying on a multi-head attention architecture described in public research papers. A competitor, which obtained a copy of the trained weights through a former employee, has argued that model weights are merely numbers produced by an automated process and therefore cannot be protected by copyright under Argentine law. The board has asked what protection the weights enjoy and what remedies are available.

Summary of Our Conclusions

1. The attention mechanism itself, as an architectural idea published in scientific literature, is not protected by copyright; ideas, methods and mathematical procedures are excluded under Law 11.723.
2. Source code implementing the model, including the attention layers, qualifies as a protected computer program under the 1998 amendment to Law 11.723, provided it reflects original creative choices.
3. Whether trained weights qualify as a protected work is unsettled in Argentine law, and no court has ruled on the point.
4. Regardless of copyright, the weights qualify as confidential information protected by Law 24.766, provided IntelSur took reasonable measures to keep them secret.
5. The former employee's confidentiality obligations under the employment contract provide an additional, independent basis for action.

Discussion

The weights of a model are determined by training data and training procedure rather than by direct human choice of each value. Authors favouring protection argue that the selection of data, the design of the architecture, and the many decisions made during training reflect creative effort. Opponents point out that copyright protects expression, not the output of an optimisation algorithm. Given this uncertainty, we advise against relying primarily on copyright.

Law 24.766 offers firmer ground. It protects information that is secret, has commercial value because it is secret, and has been subject to reasonable measures to preserve its secrecy. IntelSur's access logs, encryption of model files, and confidentiality clauses with staff appear sufficient to meet these requirements. Unauthorised acquisition or use of such information is unlawful and supports both injunctive relief and damages.

Recommendation

We recommend that IntelSur seek a precautionary injunction under Law 24.766 and the employment contract, preventing the competitor from using or distributing the weights, while reserving copyright arguments as a secondary claim. Partner Dra. Mercedes Aguirre will lead the matter and is available to meet the board this week.

Small tea
ms often put off moving a database because they imagine it requires weeks of downtime and spe

cialist consultants. In practice, moving a modest MySQL database to PostgreSQL can be done in a weekend if you prepare carefully. This tutorial uses the example of Chaiwala Express, a tea chain with 23 outlets in Jaipur and Ajmer, which moved 
its 18 gigabyte orders database last spring. The Starting Point Chaiwala Express ran a MySQL 5.7 database on a single virtual machine. It
stored menu items, outlet details, customer loyalty accounts and about 4.6 million order records. The team, led by developer Mohit Agarwal, wanted to move to PostgreSQL 16 on a

managed service to get better JSON support for the loyalty programme and to stop managing backups themselves. Step 1: Inventory the Schema Before touching data, list everything in the source database: tables, indexes, views, stored procedures, triggers and scheduled events. Chaiwala Express had 31 tables, two views and one trigger that updated loyalty points after each order. Stored logic is the hardest part to migrate automaticall
y, so note it separately. Step 2: Convert the Schema Use a tool such as pgloader to generate a first draft of the PostgreSQL schema, then review it by hand. Watch for these common differences:

- MySQL's TINYINT(1), often used for booleans, should become PostgreSQL's BOOLEAN. - AUTO_INCREMENT columns become identity columns or sequences.
- DATETIME columns usually map to TIMESTAMP, but decide explicitly whether you need time zones. - Case-insensitive text comparisons in MySQL become case-sensitive in PostgreSQL unless you use the citext extension. - Backtick-quoted identifiers
 must be changed to double quotes or left unquoted.

Chaiwala Express discovered the case sensitivity issue when testing customer search: a loyalty lookup 
for "Sharma" no longer found records stored as "SHARMA". They added citext to the name and email columns. Step 3: Rewrite Stored Logic The loyalty trigger had to be rewritten in PL/pgSQL. Mohit took the opportunity to move the logic into the application code instead, which made it easier to test. Step 4: Rehearse the Copy Run a full copy into a 
staging PostgreSQL instance and time it. For Chaiwala Express, copying the full database took 47 minutes. Run the application against staging and check every important screen, esp
ecially reports, which tend to rely on database-specific functions. Step 5: Cut Over On the chosen night, the team put the ordering app into maintenance mode at 11:30 pm after outlets closed, ran a final copy, compared row counts for every table, switched the application's connection string, and reopened at 1:15 am. They kept the MySQL server running read-only for a fortnight in case anything needed checking. What They Learned The migration itself was the easy part. Most of the effort went into finding queries that behaved differently, which is why rehearsal against real data is the step you should never skip.

Small teams often put off moving a database because they imagine it requires weeks of downtime and specialist consultants. In practice, moving a modest MySQL database to PostgreSQL can be done in a weekend if you prepare carefully. This tutorial uses the example of Chaiwala Express, a tea chain with 23 outlets in Jaipur and Ajmer, which moved its 18 gigabyte orders database last spring.

The Starting Point

Chaiwala Express ran a MySQL 5.7 database on a single virtual machine. It stored menu items, outlet details, customer loyalty accounts and about 4.6 million order records. The team, led by developer Mohit Agarwal, wanted to move to PostgreSQL 16 on a managed service to get better JSON support for the loyalty programme and to stop managing backups themselves.

Step 1: Inventory the Schema

Before touching data, list everything in the source database: tables, indexes, views, stored procedures, triggers and scheduled events. Chaiwala Express had 31 tables, two views and one trigger that updated loyalty points after each order. Stored logic is the hardest part to migrate automatically, so note it separately.

Step 2: Convert the Schema

Use a tool such as pgloader to generate a first draft of the PostgreSQL schema, then review it by hand. Watch for these common differences:

- MySQL's TINYINT(1), often used for booleans, should become PostgreSQL's BOOLEAN.
- AUTO_INCREMENT columns become identity columns or sequences.
- DATETIME columns usually map to TIMESTAMP, but decide explicitly whether you need time zones.
- Case-insensitive text comparisons in MySQL become case-sensitive in PostgreSQL unless you use the citext extension.
- Backtick-quoted identifiers must be changed to double quotes or left unquoted.

Chaiwala Express discovered the case sensitivity issue when testing customer search: a loyalty lookup for "Sharma" no longer found records stored as "SHARMA". They added citext to the name and email columns.

Step 3: Rewrite Stored Logic

The loyalty trigger had to be rewritten in PL/pgSQL. Mohit took the opportunity to move the logic into the application code instead, which made it easier to test.

Step 4: Rehearse the Copy

Run a full copy into a staging PostgreSQL instance and time it. For Chaiwala Express, copying the full database took 47 minutes. Run the application against staging and check every important screen, especially reports, which tend to rely on database-specific functions.

Step 5: Cut Over

On the chosen night, the team put the ordering app into maintenance mode at 11:30 pm after outlets closed, ran a final copy, compared row counts for every table, switched the application's connection string, and reopened at 1:15 am. They kept the MySQL server running read-only for a fortnight in case anything needed checking.

What They Learned

The migration itself was the easy part. Most of the effort went into finding queries that behaved differently, which is why rehearsal against real data is the step you should never skip.

The Ministry of Industry, Energy and Mining should require wind farm operators to file standardised maintenance and failure reports each year, starting with installations above 20 megawatts. This memo sets out why the current lack of data is becoming a problem for grid planning and what a reporting rule could look like.

Context Uruguay now has about 1,500 megawatts of installed wind capacity, spread across more than forty farms. Most were built between 2012 and 2017, which means a large share of the fleet will reach mid-life together. Gearbox replacements, blade repairs and major bearing work tend to cluster in years ten to fifteen of a turbine's life. If several large farms lose significant capacity at the same time for extended repairs, the dispatcher ADME will need to plan for it, yet at present it learns of long outages only when they happen.

What We Know and What We Do Not Operators report generation and availability, but not the causes of downtime or the components involved. Anecdotal evidence from contractors suggests that blade leading-edge erosion is more severe on farms in Maldonado and Rocha than manufacturers anticipated, likely due to salt spray and heavy rain. Without systematic reports, the ministry cannot confirm this, compare it across manufacturers, or advise on whether new projects near the coast should specify protective coatings.

Proposed Reporting Elements - Hours of downtime per turbine, separated into scheduled and unscheduled.
- The component responsible for each unscheduled stop longer than 24 hours. - Major component replacements, including gearboxes, generators, main bearings and blades.
- Planned major works for the coming twelve months, with expected duration. - Blade inspection findings, using a common five-level damage scale. Burden on Operators Most operators already hold this information in their computerised maintenance systems, so the extra effort mainly involves mapping it to a common format. We suggest a simple spreadsheet template for the first two years and a web form after that. Commercially sensitive details, such as contractor prices, would not be requested, and results would be published only in aggregated form. Next Steps

We propose consulting the Asociación Uruguaya de Energías Renovables and the three largest maintenance contractors during October, with a draft resolution ready by December. Engineer Lucía Ferrando of the National Energy Directorate has agreed to coordinate the technical working group. A first reporting cycle could cover calendar year 2027.

Syllepte subcyaneoalba is a moth in the family Crambidae. It was described by George Hampson in 1918. It is found in Cameroon.

The wingspan is about 38 mm. The forewings are very dark brown, glossed with purple. There is a faint rather diffused dark antemedial line and an indistinct dark discoidal bar. The postmedial line is faint, dark and rather diffused, erect to vein 3, then retracted to below the end of the cell and erect to the inner margin. There is a slight pale line at the base of the cilia. The hindwings are very dark brown, glossed with purple and there are traces of a dark discoidal spot and a diffused postmedial line. There is also a slight pale line at the base of the cilia.

Hluboš is a municipality and village in Příbram District in the Central Bohemian Region of the Czech Republic. It has about 700 inhabitants. Administrative parts The village of Kardavec is an administrative part of Hluboš. Geography Hluboš is located about north of Příbram and southwest of Prague. It lies in the Brdy Highlands. The highest point is the hill Malý Chlum at above sea level. The municipality is situated on the right bank of the Litavka river. History The first written mention of Hluboš is from 1355. Hluboš is a municipality and village in Příbram District in the Central Bohemian Region of the Czech Republic. It has about 700 inhabitants.

Administrative parts

The village of Kardavec is an administrative part of Hluboš.

Geography
Hluboš is located about north of Příbram and southwest of Prague. It lies in the Brdy Highlands. The highest point is the hill Malý Chlum at above sea level. The municipality is situated on the right bank of the Litavka river.

History
The first written mention of Hluboš is from 1355. A wooden fortress was located here. The owners of Hluboš often changed and belonged to the lower nobility. In 1546, Petr Vamberský had rebuilt the fortress into a castle.

Sights
The Hluboš Castle was rebuilt into the late Baroque form in the 18th century. In 1872, it was reconstructed and extended by the family of Oettingen-Wallerstein. The result of these modifications is the present appearance of the castle with many pseudo-Renaissance elements. In 1920 and 1921 it served as a summer residence of Czechoslovak president T. G. Masaryk.

The botanical garden at Hluboš Castle is one of the oldest in Central Europe. Through the Hluboš park, some trees from America and China appeared in the Czech Republic for the very first time. These were, for example, Ginkgo biloba, Cedrus libani, Juniperus virginiana, Tsuga canadensis, Thuja and Taxus.

Today the castle complex is privately owned and partially open to the public under certain conditions.

PH 4102 Public Health Practice

Lecture 5: Planning a mass vaccination campaign, using the 2025 measles catch-up in Greater Glasgow as a case. Lecturer: Professor Mhairi Buchanan, School of Health and Wellbeing.

Setting the Scene

By early 2025, uptake of the second MMR dose among five-year-olds in parts of north-east Glasgow had fallen to 81 percent, well below the 95 percent needed to prevent sustained measles transmission. After imported cases were confirmed in Springburn and Easterhouse, the health board launched a twelve-week catch-up campaign targeting children and young adults who had missed one or both doses. We will use it to illustrate the decisions any campaign planner faces.

Core Planning Questions

Every campaign has to answer the same basic questions before a single vial is opened:

* Who exactly is the target population, and how will they be identified from existing records?
* Where will vaccination take place, and how far will people need to travel?
* How will the message reach groups with low trust in health services?
* What staff, cold-chain capacity and stock are needed at peak demand?
* How will uptake be measured in near real time so the plan can be adjusted?

In Glasgow, the target list was drawn from the child health surveillance system and GP records, producing roughly 23,000 names. Clinics ran in schools, community centres and two mosques, with drop-in evening sessions at the Forge shopping centre.

What Worked and What Did Not

Uptake reached 64 percent of the target list by week twelve. School-based sessions were the most effective setting, but they missed young adults aged 16 to 24, who responded best to pharmacy appointments booked by text message. Letters alone had very little effect, and the team noticed that responses rose sharply only after trusted local figures, including a popular youth worker in Castlemilk, recorded short videos for social media.

The campaign also hit a practical snag. The first fortnight's sessions were planned around stock arriving weekly, but demand in week three exceeded supply at two sites, and families who were turned away rarely came back. The lesson is that a campaign should hold a buffer of at least one week's peak demand from the outset.

Key Takeaways

* Identify the population from records, but expect those records to be out of date.
* Match the setting to the age group rather than using one model for everyone.
* Invest early in community messengers, not just printed materials.

For next week, read the evaluation report published by Public Health Scotland and prepare a one-page critique of its outcome measures. We will discuss these in groups on Tuesday.

Wilfred Adams Russell (22 July 1874 – 8 January 1932), was an Australian politician. He was a Member of the Queensland Legislative Assembly.

Early life and education Russell was born in Queensland in 1874 and educated in New South Wales, where
he later acquired pastoral and agricultural interests. Pastoralism In 1909 he acquired an interest in Dalmally Station near Roma and took up residence there in 1910. He further extended his pastoral interests with the acquisition of properties at Cunnamulla and Jimbour Station. Jimbour was purchased from Charles Whippell. Title was transferred to Russell in January 1925. He pioneered the use of motorised livestock transport in the 1920s.

Politics Like the Bells before him, Russell of Jimbour became involved in local politics. He served as an alderman of the Dalby Town council and as the member for Dalby in the Queensland Legislative Assembly from 1926 until his death in 1932. In 1927 he donated part of the Bunya Mountains National Park to the community. In 1931 he was involved in the acquisition of part of Lake Broadwater as a national park. Family Russell was married to Millicent Baldwin of Tamworth. They had five children, 2 sons and 3 daughters. Muriel, Joan, Henry, Charles and Eileen.

Biography
Forster started working at the Schauspielhaus Zürich and in the 1970s, she toured abroad with Franz Xaver Kroetz. From 1981 to 1999, she was involved with the Residenztheater in Munich, where she studied alongside Reschii Greesa, Amélie Niermeyer, Anselm Webe and Hans Neuenfels. Nicholas More (died 1689) was first chief justice of the Province of Pennsylvania. Early life More (also spelled "Moore" or "Moor") was born in England, where he also married his wife Mary. More immigrated to the American Thirteen Colonies with William Penn in 1682 and lived in the colony of Pennsylvania, but little is known of More prior to this. It is known that More was trained in London as a medical physician, but he di
d not engage in that profession after immigration. Soon after settling in Society Hill, Philadelphia, he set up "The Free Society of Traders" and became its president. More with other English merchants obtained a parcel of land consisting of just under ten thousand (9,815) acres from Penn for the society in 1684, which became known as the Manor of Moreland. Part of the land was in Philadelphia County and part was in Montgomery County, Pennsylvania. More had a town house at the corner of Second Street and Spruce Street in Philadelphia. In addit
ion he had a country house at Green Spring, near Somerton, Philadelphia. Mid-life
More, according to tradition, became the president or speaker of the first provincial assembly of freemen of Pennsylvania. It initially assembled on 4 December 1682 at Chester, Pennsylvania. He was secretary and clerk to the provincial council in 1683. and became a member of the assembly in 1684-85. More was the presiding judge of Philadelphia county courts in 1683-84. He claimed he was an attorney in London, so Penn appointed him to become the first chief justice of the supreme court of the province of Pennsylvania in 1684. Because of his arrogant and contentious demeanor he was impeached on 15 May 1685 for "high crimes and misdemeanors", being charged with abusing his powers. He had ten charges brought against him. This was the first case in America of an impeachment of a judge. A letter containing the impeachment was forwarded to Penn, who meanwhile had gone to England. He did not give More's impeachment his official approval. Penn was still confident of More's abilities and nominated him in 1686 as one of the five commissioners for the executive branch of the Pennsylvania government. More was later given back his position as chief justice of the colony of Pennsylvania and his job as judge. More made a jail at his country home grounds at Green Spring and developed a court for hearing cases for prisoners. Later life and death Even though More was elect
ed a member of the board of five commissioners for the executive government he was unable to serve the position because of his poor health. He died in Philadelphia in 1689. He was survived by his wife and four children.

Summary of Findings: Tsubame Ride Ltd. v. Kurosaki Software K.K.

Prepared by Fujimori and Nakai Law Office for internal circulation, 22 September 2026. The dispute concerns the delayed release of the Tsubame Ride passenger application, version 4.0, which the developer Kurosaki Software contracted to deliver to app stores no later than 1 April 2026.

Background of the Dispute

Tsubame Ride, a ride-sharing operator based in Fukuoka, engaged Kurosaki Software under a fixed-price development agreement worth 48 million yen. The agreement set out four milestones and named a public release date tied to the spring tourist season. The application was eventually published on 19 June, eleven weeks late, after two rejections by an app store review team for incomplete privacy disclosures. Tsubame Ride withheld the final payment of 12 million yen and claimed lost booking revenue.

Issues Considered by the Tribunal

The arbitral tribunal, chaired by retired judge Takeshi Maruyama, framed the dispute around these questions:

• Whether the release date was a binding obligation or a target subject to store approval
• Whether the privacy disclosure failures were the developer's responsibility
• Whether lost revenue was a foreseeable consequence of the delay
• Whether the withheld payment was a lawful set-off under the agreement

Holding

The tribunal found that clause 7.2 made the release date binding but excused delays caused by third-party platform review, provided the developer submitted a compliant build in good time. Because the first submission omitted a required data-collection statement that Kurosaki had agreed in writing to prepare, the tribunal held that roughly seven of the eleven weeks of delay were attributable to the developer. The remaining four weeks arose from a second review cycle in which the store requested changes to location-permission wording supplied by Tsubame Ride itself.

On damages, the tribunal accepted that reduced bookings during Golden Week were foreseeable, since the contract recitals mentioned the holiday period explicitly. However, it reduced the claimed figure of 31 million yen to 9.6 million yen, finding that the operator's revenue projections relied on a marketing campaign that was never launched.

Practical Implications

Clients commissioning mobile applications should state clearly who prepares store compliance materials and should define how third-party review time is treated in any release deadline. Developers, for their part, ought to keep dated records of every submission and reviewer response, because the tribunal relied heavily on such logs when dividing responsibility. The net award to Kurosaki Software, after set-off, was 2.4 million yen plus interest from 1 July 2026.

HRM 2041, Week 6: Redesigning Recruitment at Scale Today we leave theory behi
nd for an hour and look at a real case. In 2025 the Dundee head office of Tay Valley Housing Association rebuilt its
hiring process from scratch after an internal review found that the average vacancy stayed open for 71 days and that almost a third of new starters left within their first year. Keep those two figures in mind, because every change we discuss today was justified against them. The Old Process Under the previous arrangement, a line manager wrote an advert, HR posted it on three job boards, and applications arrived as emailed CVs. Shortlisting depended on whoever had a free afternoon. Interviews were unstructured conversations, and different panels for the same role often asked completely different questions. Notice how many points of failure sit in that description before anyone is even hired.
What Changed The association's people director, Eili

dh MacAskill, introduced five linked reforms over a single quarter: • A standard job profile template listing essential and desirable criteria, signed off before any advert went live. • An applicant tracking system that scored applications against those criteria and logged every decision. • Anonymised shortlisting, with names, ages and addresses hidden from the first reviewer. • Structured interviews using
 the same six questions and a five-point scoring scale for every candidate.
• A two-week onboarding plan agreed with the new starter before their first day. Results After One Year Time to hire fell to 39 days, mostly because shortlisting stopped waiting for a free afternoon. First-year attr
ition dropped from 31 to 17 percent, which the association attributes partly to the onboarding plan and partly to clearer job profiles that set honest expectations. The share of shortlisted candidates from postcodes in the most deprived fifth of Dundee rose noticeably, although the sample is too small to draw firm conclusions. Points for Discussion

I want you to be sceptical here. A drop in attrition could reflect the wider labour market, since 2025 saw fewer competing vacancies in the city. Structured interviews are well supported by research, yet panels at Tay Valley reported that they felt mechanical and occasionally missed candidates
 with unusual career paths. For
seminar on Thursday, prepare a short argument on whether the gains justify the loss of flexibility, and identify one metric you would add to the evaluation if you were advising Ms MacAskill. Reading for next week: chapters four and five of the course text, plus the CIPD summary on selection methods posted on Moodle
.

• A two-week onboarding plan agreed with the new starter before their first day.

Results After One Year

Time to hire fell to 39 days, mostly because shortlisting stopped waiting for a free afternoon. First-year attrition dropped from 31 to 17 percent, which the association attributes partly to the onboarding plan and partly to clearer job profiles that set honest expectations. The share of shortlisted candidates from postcodes in the most deprived fifth of Dundee rose noticeably, although the sample is too small to draw firm conclusions.

Points for Discussion

I want you to be sceptical here. A drop in attrition could reflect the wider labour market, since 2025 saw fewer competing vacancies in the city. Structured interviews are well supported by research, yet panels at Tay Valley reported that they felt mechanical and occasionally missed candidates with unusual career paths. For seminar on Thursday, prepare a short argument on whether the gains justify the loss of flexibility, and identify one metric you would add to the evaluation if you were advising Ms MacAskill.

Reading for next week: chapters four and five of the course text, plus the CIPD summary on selection methods posted on Moodle.

Dragan J. Vučićević (; born 9 October 1973) is a Serbian journalist. He is the editor of Informer newspaper. He is known for his pro-government stance and controversial statements

Biography
Vučićević was born on 9 October 1973 in Czechoslovak Socialist Republic. He graduated in journalism from the Faculty of Political Sciences at the University of Belgrade.

In his early career, Vučićević worked for the daily newspapers Politika, Blic, Glas javnosti and Demokratija, the newspaper of the Democratic Party. In the late 1990s, Marko Milošević, the son Slobodan Milošević, threatened to kill him because of a text about the birth of his son.

In the 2000s, he was among the founders of Nacional, Kurir and Press and worked in those newspapers. Nacional was temporarily banned from publishing following the assassination of Zoran Đinđić.

In May 2012, Vučićević founded Informer, which is known for its sensationalist and biased reporting, often favoring the government and smearing the opposition, independent media, NGOs, and other perceived enemies of the regime and the ruling Serbian Progressive Party and President Aleksandar Vučić.

In 2023, he was convicted of defamation and sentenced to pay a fine of 200,000 dinars or serve a six-month prison term for insulting Jugoslav Ćosić, a former director of N1 channel.

He has six children.

Database Systems II, Session 8: Planning a Production Database Migration Notes taken by the teaching assistant, Facultad de Ciencias Físicas y Matemáticas, Universidad de Chile, for students of the evening section

Professor Isidora Navarrete opened by telling us that she had never seen a migration fail because of the database engine itself. Failures, in her experience, come from forgotten dependencies, unrealistic downtime estimates and inadequate testing. She then walked through a framework she uses with industry clients, illustrated with a migration she led for a regional electricity distributor in 2023. Phases of a Migration 1. Discovery, in which every application, report and scheduled job that touches the database is identified. 2. Assessment, in which incompatibilities between the source
and target systems are listed and estimated.
3. Conversion, covering schema, stored code and data types. 4. Testing, including functional, performance and data validation tests. 5. 
Cutover, the carefully rehearsed switch from the old database to the new one. 6. Stabilisation, during which the team monitors performance and fixes problems found in production. The Discovery Trap Navarrete spent much of the session on discovery, which she called the phase teams most often rush. In the electricity distributor's case, the IT department initially identified 14 applications using the database. After interviewing users across the company, the team found 31, including spreadsheets in the billing office with direct database connections and a reporting tool installed on a single manager's computer in Rancagua. Had those been missed, month-end billing would have failed after cutover.

Estimating Downtime She showed how to estimate downtime for a bulk data transfer: measure throughput on a
 representative subset, multiply by the total data volume, and add time for index rebuilding, validation and application restart. In her example, 600 gigabytes of data 
transferred at about 180 gigabytes per hour, but rebuilding indexes added another two and a half hours. Teams that forget index creation often find their maintenance window far too short. Validation Strategies

Row counts alone are not enough, she argued, since they will not catch truncated text or rounding errors. She recommends checksums on key columns, comparison of aggregate values such as sums of monetary amounts, and sampling of individual records for manual inspection. Assignment For next week, each group should prepare a discovery checklist for a hypothetical university enrolment system, identifying at least ten categories of dependency. We will compare lists in class and discuss which items are most commonly overlooked.

Clinical Notes in Amharic and English Technical Report AI-TR-202
6-08, Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute, Applied NLP Group. Authors: Kidus Ayalew, Wanjiru Njoroge and Hanna Teshome. Abstract

Standard transformer attention scales quadratically with sequence length, which limits its use on long documents such as hospital discharge summaries. We compared standard softmax attention with two linear-complexity alternatives on a classification task using 18,400 de-identified discharge summaries from three Addis Ababa hospitals. Linear attention reduced memory use by up to 78
percent on 4,096-token inputs, with accuracy losses of between 1.1 and 3.9 points depending on the method and language. 1 Motivation Discharge summaries 
at our partner hospitals often exceed 2,000 tokens after tokenisation, especially when they mix Amharic narrative with English medical terms. Our earlier models truncated these documents to 512 tokens, which discarded the treatment plans and follow-up instructions usually written at the end. Running full attention on the complete documents was possible on our single A100 server, but too slow and memory-intensive for the hospitals' own modest hardware, where the models will eventually run. 2 Methods Compared We trained three encoder models of identical size, 110 million parameters, differing only in their attention mechanism: * Standard softmax attention, used as the baseline * Kernel-based linear attention, which app
