Bionor Holding AS is a Norwegian biotechnology company, developing vaccines targeted at rapidly mutating virus infections such as HIV, Hepatitis C and Influenza. The company is also a leader in soy technology and has developed patented products for improved health and prevention of lifestyle-related diseases. It was founded by Cand.med. and Dr.philos. in protein and lipid research, Lars Høie.

Brands
The company was, under their name Nutri Pharma, formerly known for their soy-based product series within weight management (Nutrilett®, Scan Diet® and NutriPro®), cholesterol reduction (Abacor® and Abalon®) and menopausal and pre-menstrual symptoms (Nutri5®). The marketing and distribution rights for Nutri5 and NutriPro was in 2008 licensed to Nikken Europe for sale in 19 European countries, and in 2009 for Russia and CIS countries.
The brand Nutrilett was in 2010 sold to the Orkla-owned health-supplements firm Axellus.

After the sale of their main brands, the company have moved focus to the vaccine business after the acquisition of biotechnology company Bionor Immuno in 2010.

In 2016, the company was taken over by new investors who pivoted its business from biotech to property management, under the new name Solon.

Since January 2018, the shareholders unanimously adopted to change the name of the company from Bionor Pharma AS to Bionor Holding AS.

Products in development
Per May, Bionor Pharma has four different vaccine candidates in their product pipeline, from preclinical phase to phase II, leading to phase III which is the last phase before regulatory approval and potential market entry.

Vacc-4x
Vacc-4x aims to generate immune responses to conserved domains, regions of the virus common to all strains of HIV, even if the virus mutates. Persistent immune responses against this part of the virus (the HIV p24 protein) has been shown to delay HIV disease progression. Vacc-4x is made of modified synthetic peptides targeting these conserved regions of the HIV p24. Upon immunization with Vacc-4x, potentially followed by reboosting vaccinations, Bionor's researchers are seeking to control virus infection for a longer period of time by exercising the patient's own immune system to seek out and kill virus-producing cells.

In phase II, 134 HIV-infected people from Europe and the US participated in a randomized, placebo-controlled study, where 93 randomly selected people where to receive Vacc-4x and 43 randomly selected people received a placebo injection. The patients were injected with either placebo or Vacc-4x in 28 weeks, followed up by 24 weeks without any injection.

77 people successfully completed the study (week 52); 25 from the placebo group and 56 from the Vacc-4x group. The placebo group (n=25) had a viral load set point (average of the last two viral load measurements before the end of the study) of 61,900 HIV-RNA/copies/ml (median), compared to the Vacc-4x group (n=56) that had a viral load set point of 22,300 HIV-RNA/copies/ml (median). This difference represents a reduction of 64% and is statistically significant (p=0.04).

Bionor Pharma is in the process of conducting two further clinical studies with the Vacc-4x, which can lead towards phase III, which include 1. Vacc-4x in combination with Celgene`s immune modulator Revlimid and 2. reboosting patients from the phase II study to investigate whether this can result in a further reduction in viral load.

Thirty three patients from USA and four European countries from the last study with Vacc-4x are taking part at ten clinics. The study was approved in all participating countries in Q4 2012, with startup of patient screening soon after.

Others
Other vaccines include humoral, antibody-mediated peptide-based therapeutic HIV-1 vaccine Vacc-C5, that aims to guide the immune system to seek out and kill HIV-infected cells, Vacc-HCV, aiming to treat chronic HCV infection that affects the liver and Vacc-Flu, which is in the preclinical phase of development.

Paranda Tahsil is a tahsil (subdistrict) in Osmanabad district, Marathwada region in Maharashtra on Deccan Plateau of India. The town of Paranda is the administrative headquarters of the tahsil. There are seventy-two panchayat villages in Paranda Tahsil. Demographics In the 2001 Indian census, Paranda Tahsil had a population of 125,136, with 64,707 (51.7%) males and 60,429 (48.3%) females, for a gender ratio of 934 females per thousand males. In the 2011 census, Paranda Tahsil had 140,436 inhabitants and a gender ratio of 898 females per thousand males. The tahsil was 86.6% rural. The literacy rate in 2011 was 72.25% overall in Paranda Tahsil, with a rate of 81.32% for males and 62.29% for females. In 2011 in Paranda Tahsil, 11.8% of the population was 0 to 6 years of age. Monuments and attractions in the tahsil Sina Kolegaon (Kalyan Sagar) Dam is located near the village 
of Domgaom on the Sina River (Seena River). The reservoir is a place of scenic beauty where migratory birds can also be found. The nearby temple of Kalyan Swami, one of the beloved followers of Ramdas Swami, is now surrounded by water on three sides. The backwater of the dam extends to the village of Sonari, a popular family weekend resort.

The backwater of the dam extends to the village of Sonari, a popular family weekend resort.

Urban Transport Planning, Lecture 6: How a Railway Timetable Is Built

Notes taken by Bui Thanh Huong for the study group, Hanoi University of Civil Engineering, 3 October

Dr. Kwon Min-seok began by drawing a single line on the board from Hanoi to Hai Phong and asking us how many trains could run on it in one hour. Nobody could answer without more information, which was exactly his point. Capacity depends on signalling headway, the number of passing loops, station dwell times and the mix of fast and slow trains, and a timetable is the document where all of these constraints are made visible at once.

The Time-Distance Graph

The main tool of the lecture was the graphical timetable, sometimes called a train graph. Distance runs along the vertical axis and time along the horizontal axis, so each train appears as a sloping line. Steeper lines are faster trains, flat segments are stops, and two lines crossing on single track must cross exactly at a station with a loop, otherwise the plan is physically impossible. Dr. Kwon said French planners have used versions of this graph since the 1840s, and that the software tools at Vietnam Railways still display it in almost the same form.

Inputs a Planner Needs

• Running times between each pair of stations for every rolling stock type.
• Minimum headway allowed by the signalling system, which is around eight minutes on the Hai Phong line.
• Dwell times at each station, adjusted for expected passenger volumes.
• Locations and lengths of passing loops on single-track sections.
• Crew and rolling stock availability, including turnaround time at terminals.

Recovery Time and Robustness

A timetable that works only when every train is perfectly on time will fail within the first morning. Planners therefore add recovery time, also called slack, usually as a percentage of running time. Dr. Kwon showed data from Korail's Gyeongui Line, where adding four percent recovery cut average delay at the terminus by almost half, at the cost of making scheduled journeys about three minutes longer. He argued that passengers forgive a slightly slower schedule far more easily than a schedule that is never met.

There is a trade-off, though. Too much slack wastes capacity and makes trains wait at stations for no visible reason, which irritates riders. The usual practice is to concentrate recovery time just before major stations, so that a late train can catch up before the stop where most people board.

For Next Week

We need to draw a train graph for a fictional 60-kilometre single-track line with three passing loops, running one express and two local trains per hour in each direction. Dr. Kwon hinted that the obvious pattern will not fit and that we should consider shifting the express by a few minutes. Group meeting on Monday at 18:00 in the library, room B204, to compare attempts before the tutorial.

Joint meeting of the English and French department heads, Ottawa-Carleton District School Board, secondary panel

Held on 29 September 2026 at the board office on Greenbank Road, 16:00 to 17:30

Attendance: Margaret Leclair (curriculum superintendent, chair), Ian Robertson (Glebe Collegiate), Nathalie Poitras (Earl of March), Aaron Wiseman (Brookfield), Julie Bélanger (Lisgar Collegiate), Priya Ramesh (Merivale). Minutes: Julie Bélanger.

Purpose The meeting was called to plan the implementation of the revised Ontario grade 9 English course, which now places greater emphasis on explicit instruction in reading foundations, oral language and the analysis of texts by Indigenous, Black and other underrepresented authors. Margaret noted that while the course was introduced in 2023, many schools have adopted it unevenly, and the board wants a more consistent approach by the start of the second semester. Discussion Ian reported that teachers at his school found the new expectations around reading foundations challenging, since many secondary English teachers have little training in teaching decoding or fluency. Some students arrive in grade 9 reading several years below grade level, and teachers feel unprepared to help them. Aaron agreed and added that classroom libraries in several schools are not stocked with texts that meet the new expectations for diverse authors. Nathalie raised the question of whether the French as a second language department could share strategies, since French teachers routinely teach reading foundations to non-native speakers. Several department heads found this a useful idea and suggested joint professional development. Points of Agreement

By the end of the discussion, the group agreed on the following priorities for the second semester: - Provide a half-day training session on reading assessment for all grade 9 English teachers in November. - Allocate $2,500 per school from the board's literacy fund for classroom library purchases. - Create a shared list of recommended texts by Canadian Indigenous and Black authors, reviewed by the board's Indigenous education team. - Organise a joint session with French department heads on oral language and fluency strategies.
- Collect data on grade 9 reading levels at the start and end of the semester to measure progress. Concerns Raised Priya expressed concern that the literacy fund would not stretch far enough for schools with large grade 9 cohorts, such as Merivale, which has eleven sections. Margaret agreed to ask whether funding could be distrib
uted by enrolment rather than equally. Julie noted that teachers had been asked to adapt to several curriculum changes in a short period and that workload should be considered when scheduling training.

Next Steps Margaret will circulate a draft training agenda by 13 October. Department heads will consult their teachers on text recommendations and send suggestions to Julie by 20 October. The next meeting will be held on 3 November at the same location.

Nazi Germany invaded France in May 1940. Their rapid advance through the undefended Ardennes caused a crisis in the French government; the French Third Republic dissolved itself in July, and handed over absolute power to Marshal Philippe Pétain, an elderly hero of World War I. Pétain signed an armistice with Germany with the nor
th and west of France under German military occupation. Pétain, charged with calling a Constitutional Authority, instead established an authoritarian government in the spa town of Vichy, in the southern zone libre ("free zone"). Though nominally independent, Vichy France became a collaborationist regime and was little more than a Nazi client state that actively participated in Jewish deportations. Even before France 
surrendered on 22 June 1940, General Charles
de Gaulle fled to London, from where he called on his fellow citizens to resist the Germans. The British recognized and funded Free French government in exile based in London. Efforts to liberate France began in the autumn of 1940 in France's colonial empire in Africa, still in the hands of the Vichy regime. General persuaded French Chad to support Free France, and by 1943 most other French colonies in Equatorial and North Africa had followed suit. announced formation
of the Empire Defense Council in Brazzaville, which became the capital of Free France. Allied military efforts in north western Europe began in summer 1944 with two seaborne invasions of France. Operation Overlord in June 1944 landed two million men, including a French armoured division, through the beaches of Normandy, opening a Western front against Germany. Operation Dragoon in August launched a second offensive force, including French Army B, from the département of Algeria into southern France. City after city in France was liberated, and even Paris was liberated on 25 August 1944. As the liberation progressed, resistance groups were incorporated into the Allied strength. In September, under threat of the Allied advance Pétain and the remains of the Vichy regime fled into exile in Germany. A few pockets of German resistance remained in control of the

Immediately after liberation, France was swept by a wave of executions, assaults, and degradation of suspected collaborators, including shaming of women suspected of relationships with Germans. Some defendants received death sentences, and faced a firing squad.
